title: Core–chalcogen substitution in tub-shaped carbon nanobelts: a DFT study on structural mechanics, electronic thresholds, and charge transport parameters
content: Core-heteroatom engineering offers a powerful paradigm for modulating the electronic thresholds and supramolecular topologies of non-planar, shape-persistent macrocycles without disrupting their conjugated carbon skeletons. Herein, we present a systematic density functional theory (DFT) study investigating the structural mechanics, charge-transport dynamics, and vibrational profiles of tub-shaped carbon nanobelt macrocycles (C48H16X, where X = S8−nSen) across the B3P86/6-31G(d,p) and B3LYP/6-31G(d,p) levels of theory. Descending from the octathia (S8) to the octaselena (Se8) core drives a continuous physical expansion of the internal base diameter (8.82 → 9.19 Å), forcing an inward tilt of the polycyclic walls that steepens the cavity profile and compresses the macrocyclic cone angle by 10.9° (48.7° → 37.8°). Homodesmotic reaction modeling demonstrates that this radial expansion mitigates local bending stress, lowering normalized curvature strain from 15.88 kcal per mol per unit to 12.87 kcal per mol per unit, In heteroleptic isomers (C48H16S4Se4), total strain behaves as a colligative thermodynamic property (∼14.39 to 12.87 kcal per mo per unit), whereas spatial sequencing dictates local desymmetrization, producing wave-like, ellipsoidal, pear-shaped, or asymmetric projections. Electronically, mixing high-energy Se(4p) lone pairs into the π-system destabilizes the HOMO, systematically reducing the vertical ionization potential (IPv) by up to 0.350 eV and elevating the vertical electron affinity (EAv) by 0.146 eV while leaving the carbon-centered LUMO invariant. Crucially, the intrinsic structural rigidity of the symmetric homoleptic (1, 6) and alternating heteroleptic (2) macrocyclic frames restricts nuclear reorganization during charge hopping, preserving low inner-sphere hole (λh ∼0.165–0.182 eV) and electron (λe ∼0.247–0.271 eV) barriers. In contrast, spatial desymmetrization in block-paired and asymmetric isomers (3–5) induces localized steric distortions that elevate reorganization barriers, particularly for electron transport (λe ∼0.389–0.590 eV). Harmonic IR spectra reveal distinct spectroscopic markers: carbon backbone breathing modes redshift by 15–25 cm−1 due to enhanced electron donation, local C–S modes (680–740 cm−1) give way to low-energy C–Se vibrations (500–580 cm−1), and symmetry breaking lifts vibrational degeneracy into distinct doublets. These findings establish core chalcogen substitution as a precise design tool for engineering low-barrier, ambipolar organic semiconductors. However, we note that our present investigation is strictly limited to the single-molecule scale; these low reorganization barriers highlight an intrinsic intramolecular potential for low-barrier charge transport, while comprehensive solid-state dimer-level, transfer integral, and crystal packing calculations are under consideration and will be published elsewhere.
